🚨 A 6-year-old girl was rescued alive after spending approximately 55 to 60 hours trapped beneath flood debris in Timure, Rasuwa District, Nepal. Members of Nepal’s Armed Police Force worked through mud and wreckage before reaching the child, identified in reports as Manisha, and safely pulling her from the destruction. 🙏 The girl received immediate medical assistance and was reportedly transferred to Kathmandu for further care. Namche Bazaar, Nepal, sits 11,300 feet up in the Himalayas — and no road reaches it. So everything the town needs is carried up on human backs, the loads held by a single strap stretched across each porter's forehead. Scientists who weighed porters right on the trail found men hauling almost their entire body weight up the mountain. The secret isn't just toughness — Sherpas' muscles use oxygen more efficiently than most people's, letting them thrive where the air is dangerously thin. And the story runs even deeper, into their DNA. Many Sherpas carry a gene variant inherited from the Denisovans, a vanished people who once lived across Asia and disappeared long ago. That single gene may be part of what lets them live and work at altitudes that leave outsiders gasping. But a mystery remains: no one knows exactly where these two peoples crossed paths. Did the ancestors of the Sherpas meet the Denisovans high on the plateau itself, already adapted to the heights — or did that fateful mixing happen far below, long before anyone climbed this high? Did their ancestors meet the Denisovans high on the plateau, or far below it? 👇 #AI #mystery #didyouknow #unexplained #Nepal

November 14, 2026 Gorkha District, Nepal A large dry landslide occurred in Gorkha District. A mass of earth and rock collapsed from the Gundrung Pakha slope into the Thado Bharyang forest area near Yarubagar. Rocks began falling as early as Friday night, and the main landslide took place around 8:30 a.m., kicking up a massive cloud of dust. Debris reached the Budhi Gandaki River. The landslide blocked both a motorable road and a foot trail. According to the district police, there were no casualties or material damage.

The situation in Nepal remains devastating. The amount of mud and debris is overwhelming, and the work is challenging. But our team continues working alongside the local communities, doing everything we can to salvage as many belongings as possible from the rubble and disinfect homes to make them safe again. Sunita is one of the many homeowners our team has met along the way. She remains in her home, carefully cleaning, salvaging what is valuable to her, and gathering the belongings she hopes to recover. Every item saved is a little piece of her life and memories preserved. We’re still here doing our best to support as many families as possible.
